column4: Visit note | 2025-02-08 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Shirin Chowdhury, 66, female. Mrs. Chowdhury reports feeling dizzy whenever she looks up and experiences brief spinning sensations when turning over in bed. She mentions that these symptoms began after a viral cold in Kushtia. She works as a shopkeeper and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies double vision, numbness, or falls. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 127/81 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 58 kg. Neurological examination is otherwise intact. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
